question: A 35-year-old woman from San Francisco has been refusing to vaccinate her children due to the claims that vaccinations may cause autism in children. Her 10-year-old male child began developing a low-grade fever with a rash that started on his face; as the rash began to spread to his limbs, it slowly disappeared from his face. When the child was taken to a clinic, the physician noticed swollen lymph nodes behind the ears of the child. Which of the following are characteristics of the virus causing these symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "10-year-old male child" -> "developing low-grade fever" -> "rash starting on face" -> "rash spreading to limbs" -> "swollen lymph nodes behind ears" -> "symptoms consistent with viral infection" -> "likely caused by a virus associated with rash and fever" -> "characteristics suggest a nonenveloped virus" -> "possible nonenveloped, SS linear DNA" -> 75%

CHAIN: "10-year-old male child" -> "developing low-grade fever" -> "rash starting on face" -> "rash spreading to limbs" -> "swollen lymph nodes behind ears" -> "symptoms suggestive of a viral exanthem" -> "common viral causes include measles or rubella" -> "measles virus is enveloped, SS - nonsegmented RNA" -> "rubella virus is also enveloped, SS - nonsegmented RNA" -> "characteristics suggest an enveloped virus" -> 85%

CHAIN: "10-year-old male child" -> "developing low-grade fever" -> "rash starting on face" -> "rash spreading to limbs" -> "swollen lymph nodes behind ears" -> "symptoms indicate a viral etiology" -> "considering common childhood viruses" -> "measles virus is a strong candidate" -> "measles virus is enveloped, SS - nonsegmented RNA" -> 90%
analysis: The symptoms described, including low-grade fever, rash that starts on the face and spreads, and swollen lymph nodes, are characteristic of rubella, which is caused by the rubella virus. The rubella virus is an enveloped virus with single-stranded positive-sense RNA. Therefore, the correct option is one that describes an enveloped, single-stranded RNA virus.
